item.title: Syria’s Post-Assad Pulse Check
item.description: In December 2024, forces led by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham defeated Assad regime forces, leading to the regime’s collapse and raising hopes for an end to Syria’s brutal civil war. item.title: Gilded Capability: Overinvestment and the Survivability Paradox
item.description: Infernos raged aboard Japanese aircraft carriers after U.S. Navy dive-bombers found their marks during the Battle of Midway. item.title: Running to Stand Still: Russian Nuclear Modernization after New START
item.description: John Maynard Keynes once wrote, “The difficulty lies, not in the new ideas, but in escaping from the old ones”: an apt depiction of the current discourse and debate of what the world will look like now that the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START) treaty has expired. item.title: The Sound of Munich: Autonomy, Anxiety, and the Twilight of Transatlantic Order
item.description: Munich was warmer than Washington this weekend, both in weather and in sentiment. Neither development was widely forecast.
